content.text: The change updates the subscription, but several product paths read a separate organization plan field. I’m checking those readers and the event handlers so the explanation reflects what actually changes, including any divergence.

content.text:
The plan change writes the new plan to the **subscription**, but it does not update `organizations.plan`. That distinction matters: billing quota checks use the subscription as their authority, while several other product paths still read the organization’s older plan. A successful downgrade can therefore produce different answers in different parts of the product.

The sequence is:

1. In [the billing page](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/6fe98fe3-fa2d-407e-87e3-c256ef7b1482/src/app/(dashboard)/[orgSlug]/settings/billing/page.tsx), `Page` loads the tenant and checks `org:manage_billing`. Its `selectPlan` function calls `changePlanAction` with the chosen plan and a monthly interval. [BillingPlanCard](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/6fe98fe3-fa2d-407e-87e3-c256ef7b1482/src/components/domain/billing/billing-plan-card.tsx) also disables the switch button if `can` denies that permission.

   [withAction](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/6fe98fe3-fa2d-407e-87e3-c256ef7b1482/src/actions/_lib/with-action.ts) first parses the request with `changePlanSchema`, then resolves an authenticated actor for the supplied organization. The action checks `can` again. In [permissions.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/6fe98fe3-fa2d-407e-87e3-c256ef7b1482/src/lib/permissions.ts), the role matrix requires an owner for `org:manage_billing`; platform staff can also pass, but only after the cross-tenant check. The service repeats the organization-scope and permission checks.

2. In [change-plan.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/6fe98fe3-fa2d-407e-87e3-c256ef7b1482/src/actions/billing/change-plan.ts), `assertPlanFitsCurrentUsage` reads the stored usage counters through `getUsage` and compares seats, projects and storage against the **target** plan’s limits. [plan-limits.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/6fe98fe3-fa2d-407e-87e3-c256ef7b1482/src/config/plan-limits.ts) defines the limits; `wouldExceedLimit` tests `used + requested > limit`, with a requested delta of zero here. Equality is allowed.

   [billing-service.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/6fe98fe3-fa2d-407e-87e3-c256ef7b1482/src/server/services/billing-service.ts) then runs its own check in `changePlan`: it compares the target limits with seats, projects, storage and the current webhook endpoint count. An excess rejects the change before the subscription is updated. These checks run for any selected plan, not only when the code has classified it as a downgrade. The usage values are cached counters from `usage-repository.getUsage`, not a fresh recount; the change check does not test issues per project or API requests.

3. After the checks, `changePlan` calls `updateSubscriptionPlan` in [subscription-repository.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/6fe98fe3-fa2d-407e-87e3-c256ef7b1482/src/server/repositories/subscription-repository.ts). It updates the `subscriptions` row’s `plan`, `interval`, `status` to `active`, and `updatedAt`; setting the status active ends a trial. It does not update the organization row. `planFor` in the billing service reads `subscriptions.plan` first and falls back to `organizations.plan` only if no subscription exists. The update itself requires an existing subscription.

4. `changePlan` emits `billing.plan_changed` with the actor and old and new plans. When listeners are registered, `registerActivityListeners` in [activity-service.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/6fe98fe3-fa2d-407e-87e3-c256ef7b1482/src/server/services/activity-service.ts) records an activity entry, and `registerWebhookListeners` in [webhook-service.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/6fe98fe3-fa2d-407e-87e3-c256ef7b1482/src/server/services/webhook-service.ts) queues deliveries for enabled endpoints subscribed to that event. [event-bus.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/6fe98fe3-fa2d-407e-87e3-c256ef7b1482/src/lib/event-bus.ts) waits for listeners but isolates their failures. The action then revalidates the organization tag, and `withAction` revalidates the billing tag. The page’s `selectPlan` awaits but discards the action result, including a refusal.

Outside billing, `checkLimit` in the billing service now uses the new subscription plan. The [dashboard layout](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/6fe98fe3-fa2d-407e-87e3-c256ef7b1482/src/app/(dashboard)/[orgSlug]/layout.tsx) supplies its seat and project checks to the client, the [members settings page](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/6fe98fe3-fa2d-407e-87e3-c256ef7b1482/src/app/(dashboard)/[orgSlug]/settings/members/page.tsx) supplies a seat check to `InviteMemberForm`, and the [usage API](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/6fe98fe3-fa2d-407e-87e3-c256ef7b1482/src/app/api/orgs/[orgId]/usage/route.ts) returns subscription-based checks. For example, the invite form can disable invitations when that seat check says the smaller plan is full.

Other paths do **not** automatically pick up the downgrade, because they read `org.plan`, which this action leaves unchanged. Those include the actual invitation, project, issue, attachment and webhook creation guards in their respective action and service files; `buildFlagContext` in [feature-flag-service.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/6fe98fe3-fa2d-407e-87e3-c256ef7b1482/src/server/services/feature-flag-service.ts); webhook delivery eligibility in [webhook-delivery-job.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/6fe98fe3-fa2d-407e-87e3-c256ef7b1482/src/server/jobs/webhook-delivery-job.ts); and the retention window in [cleanup-archived-job.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/6fe98fe3-fa2d-407e-87e3-c256ef7b1482/src/server/jobs/cleanup-archived-job.ts). Likewise, `usePlanLimits` returns limits derived from `org.plan` alongside subscription-based checks. The usage API can consequently return an older top-level plan and limits alongside checks for the new plan, and even the billing page’s current-plan label reads `org.plan`.
